A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the afterglow evolution in a preejected stellar wind is more complex than in a homogeneous medium and, in general, the afterglow behavior is more difficult to understand in the former case.

the optical and X-ray afterglows from a GRB interacting with a homogeneous external medium are characterized by a single break, which could be either a cooling break or a synchrotron self-absorption break, depending on the observing frequency and time.

the afterglow observations at submillimetre frequencies during the first days after a GRB, together with the optical and X-ray afterglow light curves during the first hours after a GRB are the best tools to discriminate between homogeneous and wind external media.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a GRB reminant interacting with a preekected wind should produce a synchrotron spectrum that is softer at early times than at later times, and the IC upscattered radiation should be detected in soft X-ray observations of GRB remnants running in denser external media.
, in general, it is not possible to infer the nature of the external medium from a single afterglow light curve.

, in order to understand GRB afterglows, it is necessary to take into account all the relevant physical processes, including IC upscattering of photons from the external medium, and to compare the results with observations at all frequencies.
